differences.title: 1. PRIMARY LANE
differences.leftDesc: Biome targets JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystems with integrated formatting and linting. It parses modern syntax into an AST, runs rule checks, and prints deterministic output, often eliminating separate Prettier/ESLint setup.
differences.rightDesc: Ruff focuses on Python code quality via a rule-based linter. It parses Python into an AST, applies configurable checks (including many from flake8 and other tools), and emits fast diagnostics designed for CI and large repos.

differences.title: 2. ANALYSIS ENGINE
differences.leftDesc: Biome’s engine couples parsing, linting, and printing. It computes fixes/edits through the AST and format graph, aiming for consistent diffs. Under the hood, it shares structure between checks to reduce redundant work.
differences.rightDesc: Ruff is engineered for rapid rule evaluation: it selects only enabled rules, then runs targeted analyses over the AST. It minimizes overhead by structuring linting passes around rule categories and often avoids expensive inference.

differences.title: 3. AUTO-FIX BEHAVIOR
differences.leftDesc: Biome can apply formatting fixes and many lint autofixes in one workflow. Because it owns formatting, it can coordinate whitespace, semicolons, and code structure consistently, producing fewer churny diffs than mixing unrelated formatters.
differences.rightDesc: Ruff supports autofix for a subset of rules, converting diagnostics into concrete code transformations. It emphasizes predictable edits, but some checks remain “diagnostic-only” to avoid behavior-changing refactors.

differences.title: 4. CONFIG & PRESETS
differences.leftDesc: Biome uses a cohesive configuration model to control formatting options and lint rules together. Profiles can be applied per workspace, keeping JS/TS formatting and checks aligned without requiring multiple external config layers.
differences.rightDesc: Ruff config is organized around rule selection (e.g., “E”, “F”, “B”, “I” families) and explicit enable/disable sets. This makes it easy to replicate flake8-like behavior while tuning strictness across teams and CI stages.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Biome emphasizes quick turnaround by using efficient parsing/printing and avoiding multi-tool orchestration. In typical use, it can format and lint in a single invocation, reducing startup overhead and repeated AST builds.
differences.rightDesc: Ruff is built for speed in monorepos: it can lint many files concurrently and caches intermediate results across runs depending on workflow. It’s designed to keep CI times low even when enabling large rule sets.

differences.title: 6. LANGUAGE COVERAGE & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Biome is deeply integrated with JavaScript/TypeScript syntax realities: ESM/CJS patterns, TS type syntax, and modern JS constructs. It also plugs into editor/build workflows common in JS stacks for formatter-and-linter parity.
differences.rightDesc: Ruff covers Python syntax and style across typical production patterns, including checks that integrate with import sorting, common error-prone patterns, and typing-adjacent conventions. It pairs naturally with Python dependency tooling and CI linters.

differences.title: 7. BEST-FIT WORKFLOWS
differences.leftDesc: Choose Biome when you want formatting correctness and lint checks to share the same AST/printing logic, reducing churn. It’s strong for teams standardizing style across frontend/backend TypeScript repos with fewer tools.
differences.rightDesc: Choose Ruff when you want enforceable Python guardrails with granular rule codes and high-throughput linting. It excels for CI enforcement, incremental adoption, and large codebases where keeping lint costs low is crucial.
